title: How do two triangles give the area of a rhombus?
description: A rhombus has diagonals of ten and six centimetres. One diagonal splits it into two triangles on the same base, the area of each comes from half the other diagonal, and the two areas add up. Keeko doubts this and multiplies the two diagonals.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal splits a rhombus into two triangles on the same base, and their heights are halves of the other diagonal. Watch for students who use the whole other diagonal as the height.

source: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 6 cm. Find its area using
video_script.why: The child sees that the two triangles made by one diagonal each have the height of half the other diagonal, so the area is half of the product of the diagonals.
video_script.substitution: Take one diagonal as the base of both triangles and half the other diagonal as the height of each.
video_script.anchor: the book's rhombus ABCD with the diagonal BD splitting it into two triangles
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the two whole diagonals, ten times six, as if the whole second diagonal were a height.
video_script.payoff_line: The area of the rhombus is thirty square centimetres
maths_rules: rhombus ABCD: BD = 10 cm and AC = 6 cm cross at O at right angles and halve each other; AO = OC = 3 cm
triangle ABD: base BD = 10 cm, height AO = 3 cm, area = 1/2 × 10 × 3 = 15 cm²; triangle CBD is the same, 15 cm²
Keeko: 10 × 6 = 60, twice the area, because each height is 3 cm, not 6 cm
video_script.design: One rhombus all video: one diagonal makes two triangles on a common base, and the other diagonal gives their heights.

<bookmark mark='ht'/>The diagonals cut each other in half at a right angle.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>The heights eigh O and C O are equal, and each is half of six, which is three.

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, the triangle eigh B D has half of ten times three, which is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='c'/>The triangle C B D has the same base and height, so its area is fifteen as well.

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, the two triangles together make the whole rhombus.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add their areas, fifteen plus fifteen, to get thirty.

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check it. Half of the two diagonals multiplied is half of ten times six.
<bookmark mark='same'/>That is thirty too.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The area of the rhombus is thirty square centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the area is sixty square centimetres, because ten times six is sixty.
<bookmark mark='ht'/>But the height of each triangle is only three, not six.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Half of ten times three is fifteen, and two triangles give thirty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Sixty is twice the area of the rhombus.
